key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings on Grade 2 titanium achieved the best tribological performance at O2/C2H2 ratios of 3.0–3.3, where phase composition and adhesion were most favorable.
engineering_relevance: These coatings can improve wear resistance, surface durability, and biocompatibility of titanium implants in physiological environments.
method: Deposited hydroxyapatite on commercially pure Grade 2 titanium by detonation spraying.
Varied the O2/C2H2 ratio from 2.6 to 3.7 to tune coating formation.
Characterized phase structure and tribological behavior under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: X-ray diffraction showed predominant hydroxyapatite with some α-tricalcium phosphate, and tribology tests showed the lowest wear volume and best friction behavior for coatings made at O2/C2H2 = 3.0 and 3.3.
watch_item: Detonation spraying can induce phase changes and structural heterogeneity, so process control is critical to avoid degraded coating consistency.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
